pr_title: drivers: spi: make SPI dt-spec macros compatible with C++
pr_body:
As of today it is not possible to use SPI dt-spec macros in C++, something known and documented. The main reason is because `cs` property is initialized using a compound literal, something not supported in C++. This PR takes another approach, that is to not make `cs` a pointer but a struct member. This way, we can perform a regular initialization, at the cost of using extra memory for unused delay/pin/flags if `cs` is not used.

Fixes #56572
Closes #57025
pr_comments:
> LGTM - just wondering if this falls under the category of a breaking / tree-wide change and if it needs to go through some process.

Hmm I'm not sure if it applies, since the changes are restricted to something that applications should not use (we should actually isolate internals better here).

Architecture WG:

- @gmarull explains that the changes are required for C++, but the downside is that we have to allocate the structure instead of the pointer
- @teburd reiterates that this still is a public API, even if the application is never supposed to access it
- @gmarull suggests adding inline function helpers to access the CS structure
- No objections

> Can this be done as a deprecation of the old "interface" and intro a new Kconfig for the new means and have the various in-trees select that new kconfig?

Adding a Kconfig to preserve the old behavior can be done, I think. I'd not pollute tree with that symbol, though, but offer it to the apps that want to migrate later. But, as I said, despite this being in a public header, the CS field should exclusively be used by drivers, not applications. We should one day isolate better what is driver-facing and application-facing in driver headers because to me, it's not the same to change one side or the other.

issue_context.title: SPI_DT_SPEC_GET compatibility with C++
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The [`SPI_DT_SPEC_GET`](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/apidoc/latest/group__spi__interface.html#gaec6a8fde1c3ec6349a601a2d5f7af785) macro is not available in C++. It seems caused by the `SPI_CS_CONTROL_PTR_DT`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Maybe convert the `cs` so it is not a pointer, to be able to generate the proper macros with C++ compatibility.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Maybe, a workaround can be documented explaining how to define those parameters with the current implementation.

review_comments:
This is a breaking API change and needs to go through the process. If an out of tree driver implements and uses spi_config today, and goes to update zephyr, this will break that code.

I'm 100% fine with this change myself (though @tbursztyka will need to +1 it). But it needs to be announced on the mailing list and at least be brought up in the architecture meeting.

If we go this road, I'd also improve isolation of this module. Applications should, in most cases, not play with `cs` field directly. Some helper function would have been useful to prevent a breaking change here.

Unfortunately spi_config is a public struct in a public header, so even with helpers there's no guarantees. It's something we need to live with and work with. The process here is really about, making sure the community is ok with it and getting the word out.

That's ok, a quick blurb in the architecture meeting and an email. Easy

Just caught this with the arch meeting and wanted to mention it here too.

The old spi macro declaration appears to be a statement expr(ession). It's a gcc-ism (just happens to be supported by clang too), but they aren't ISO C or C++. We (somewhat unfortunately) do have them all over the place still.

I would say that the preferred way is to embed the struct, which is what Gerrard has done. We pay the price in terms of an extra 4 bytes, but it's at least ISO C / C++.

https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Statement-Exprs.html
